title: Declarative Traffic Rule Builder and Safety Briefing (prototype)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Operators need a concise, guardrailed way to express traffic routing policies (percentage splits, cohort targeting, prioritization, and emergency fallbacks) without hand-editing YAML or managing long lists of ad-hoc toggles. Current manual split UI leads to configuration errors and slow incident response.

Goal: Ship a design prototype for a declarative traffic rule builder integrated into the Redwood Console rollouts flow. The builder should: 1) let PM/engineers author human-readable rules (e.g., '10% new-model to beta users in EU when response-latency < 300ms'), 2) show a live simulation/preview and cost estimate, 3) surface safety assertions and auto-suggested rollback actions when signals cross thresholds, and 4) provide an immutable 'safety briefing' summary for audit and handoff.

Scope: Console UI surfaces (rule editor, preview/sim, safety briefing modal, failure-mode banner, and quick-escape rollback action). Prototype covers desktop and tablet interactions for the authoring flow and the emergency rollback microjourney. Not in scope: full backend rule language parsing (stubbed) and long-term audit storage UX (placeholder links to activity log).

Success metrics: 1) usability test task completion >= 90% for writing a simple cohort rule, 2) time to author + validate rule reduced by 40% vs. baseline, 3) perceived confidence score (post-task SUS-like question) >= 4/5 for safety-critical actions.
comments: 2026-02-13 - Maya Chen: Initial sketching session complete. Two variants created: (A) block-based rule composer (drag/drop predicates) and (B) single-line declarative DSL editor with live validation. Decided to prototype both for moderated usability tests.

2026-02-18 - Arjun Patel: Engineering checked feasibility for variant A (block composer) — continuous preview requires new simulation endpoint; we can mock responses for prototype. Variant B leverages existing parser service but needs clearer microcopy around predicate language. Engineering preference: start with block composer to eliminate syntax errors during authoring.

2026-02-20 - Product Feedback (Ishaan Rao): Add explicit 'safety assertions' list in the right rail showing signals we watch (latency P95, error-rate-1m, token-cost-delta) and recommended thresholds. Also request cost delta estimate for split percentages to help cost-aware decisions.

2026-02-24 - Design critique: Simplify primary CTA to 'Run preview' and add ephemeral toast mechanics for long-running simulation. Concern about cognitive load: compress predicate creation into labeled chips rather than freeform text inputs. Agreed to test 3-predicate limit in prototype.

2026-02-26 - Accessibility review (Lina Gomez): Ensure predicate chips are keyboard-navigable and support ARIA live regions for preview simulation results. Color contrast adjustments made for safety badge states (ok/warn/critical).

2026-02-28 - Research plan (Maya): Recruit 6 console power users and 6 PM/engineers who previously performed rollouts. Tasks: author basic 10% canary to segment 'mobile:android' in EU; author conditional rule with latency gate; trigger simulated metric breach and perform rollback. Record time and confidence. Prototype changes after round 1 will address language comprehension and rollback discoverability.

2026-03-01 - Arjun: Frontend prototype PR opened (link in attachments). Mock backend hooked to simulate three signals and to return suggested rollback actions based on threshold violations. Need design decision on how aggressive auto-suggested rollbacks should be presented — inline suggestion vs modal confirmation.

2026-03-01 - Maya: Preparing In Review artifacts. Requesting design + eng sign-off for the block-composer interactions and safety briefing copy. Next steps: run moderated usability tests week of 2026-03-08, iterate microcopy, and align with security on audit language if tests validate flow.
design_decisions: Choose block-based composer as primary prototype to minimize syntax errors and lower barrier to entry for non-engineering operators.
Expose three canonical safety signals in the right rail: latency (P95), error rate (1m), and cost delta. These cover reliability and economics.
Preview runs are explicit (user clicks 'Run preview') and show deterministic sample cohorts in a modal with traffic distribution visualization and cost estimate.

Rollback actions are presented as 'Suggested Actions' with recommended severity (soft-rollforward, staged-decrease, immediate-revert). Immediate-revert requires secondary confirmation and shows estimated impact.
Safety briefing is an immutable snapshot summary (exportable PDF) created when the rollout is started; prototype uses a 'snapshot now' CTA and links to activity log.
Limit predicate complexity in first iteration to 3 predicates to avoid combinatorial explosion and to keep preview table readable.
Accessibility: predicate chips keyboard focus order left-to-right, ARIA labels for safety status, and color+icon redundancy for alerts.
Telemetry: add hooks for tracking 'preview-run', 'safety-briefing-open', 'rollback-click' and 'rollback-confirm' to measure operator behaviour during incidents.
Fallback during backend unavailability: builder shows last-known-good preview and a clear offline banner; changes can be saved as draft but cannot be applied.
Microcopy: use explicit safety phrasing (e.g., 'If P95 latency > 350ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute intervals, reduce new-model traffic by 50%') to reduce ambiguity during incident response.
next_steps: Run two rounds of moderated usability tests (3 tasks each) and synthesize findings by 2026-03-15.
Incorporate research changes into Figma prototype and hand off to frontend for iterative integration tests (ENG-6312).
Create a short ops playbook doc that pairs with the safety briefing export describing escalation steps and pre-approved rollback thresholds.
Coordinate with Security on audit wording for immutable safety briefing and confirm retention policy requirements.
Add an internal design walkthrough with Growth and SRE to align on cost-estimation signals and acceptable defaults before broader rollout.
After successful tests, schedule an engineering spike to implement simulation endpoint and sampling cohort generator (ENG-6230).
